The Roles view: every Role of Server.ServerCapabilities.RoleSet with the accounts it is granted to, read via the identity mapping rules (Part 18 4.4.3). Admin-gated (WIN_REQUIRES_ADMIN), read-only. THEME-GATED, so reshell-theme rather than auto-view: MakeRolesGridPanel() returns nullptr under the legacy theme (the whole user_access panel family does), so RolesView::Init builds no widget, OpenedView::Init throws 'Can't create widget', and the view never opens. Tagged auto-view until 2026-08-02, which made every default-pipeline run fail this capture - the admin gate was NOT the cause, the session holds Configure. To publish it, the panel factory must first drop its legacy gate (the publish subset admits auto-* only). KNOWN FIXTURE GAP: Members renders 'None' for every Role. The RoleSet and its Roles browse correctly - the capture shows both - but the identity-rule rows the fixture projects under them do not come back from the client browse, so no membership reaches the view. The read path itself is unit-tested against FakeNodeService (role_membership_unittest.cpp); it is the offline fixture's rule projection that is unproven. Fix that before publishing this image. The manual prose for this surface is written (scada-docs client/workbench.md + en/ mirror, #administration); the image is NOT embedded yet because the published set must come from the WINDOWS pipeline - a macOS render differs by font alone and would commit as churn. Embed it on the next Windows regeneration, set published:true and add it to current_generator_owned_subset. CAPTURED STANDALONE since 2026-08-08 (SaveRolesScreenshot / SaveUsersGridScreenshot in user_access_capture.cpp), not through the view path: the grid is built from the server's published role->permission map, which needs ReadRolePermissions, and the generator's ordinary session is anonymous - so the view-path capture rendered 'No data' over an empty grid. AuthenticatedAttributeService supplies the administrator identity for these captures only. The member/role columns were additionally empty until a client fix the same day (ReadRoleMemberships did not fetch the rule type's chain, so no identity mapping rule read back); the tracked PNG still predates both and will change on the next Windows regeneration.

The fixture configures no policy, so the capture shows the unconstrained case (Any length, nothing required) - which is a REAL state and deliberately distinct from 'No data', the unreadable case that also suppresses every requirement row. The manual prose for this surface is written (scada-docs client/workbench.md + en/ mirror, #administration); the image is NOT embedded yet because the published set must come from the WINDOWS pipeline - a macOS render differs by font alone and would commit as churn. The Audit log view: the event journal scoped to the AuditEventType subtree (see client/modules/events/audit_events.h). Admin-gated. The capture demonstrates the filter rather than asserting it - the fixture seeds 13 events of which 4 carry audit types, and only those 4 appear. Acknowledgement chrome is deliberately absent (no unacknowledged-only toggle, no Acknowledge-all footer): an audit entry records that something happened, and there is nothing to acknowledge. The users-admin RBAC inspector (right region of users-admin.html) for the fixture's Администратор. Rewritten 2026-08-01 onto the ROLE model: it lists the Roles the account holds and derives the permission breakdown from them through the same default role->permission map the server enforces with, replacing the coarse Administrator/Operator/Observer pill that read the retired AccessRights bitmask - a pill that would have kept asserting authority for an account whose Role had been revoked. Three states stay distinct: the Roles list, 'None' (holds no Role - real, and grants nothing), and 'No data' (the RoleSet could not be read, which also suppresses every permission row). The Roles list is real as of 2026-08-08: this capture shows Operator, ConfigureAdmin. It showed 'None' until then, which was a CLIENT bug rather than a fixture gap - ReadRoleMemberships resolved a rule's Criteria through the type's property declarations without fetching the type chain, so every rule read back empty against the real node model (regression test: ScreenshotGenerator.RolesEnumerateTheirMembers). SECOND FIXTURE FACT, easy to trip over: the panel now READS what each Role grants from the server (the RolePermissions attribute, Part 3 5.2.9) instead of carrying its own map, and that attribute requires ReadRolePermissions. The generator wires the real attribute service straight into the client, so the client's empty ServiceContext -- which a real server would have replaced with the session's identity -- reads as ANONYMOUS and the attribute is refused, collapsing the whole panel to 'No data'. AuthenticatedAttributeService supplies the administrator identity for this capture only; do not widen it to the generator's other services, which would change UserAccessLevel narrowing and with it every writability affordance.

Custom table (the CusTable window, SheetModel) — the free-form spreadsheet: literal labels beside '=<formula>' cells bound to live values, with a coloured title and header band. Untagged until 2026-08-01, so the managed-image gate skipped it, and the render was a blank grid: a sheet's content lives in its saved window as SheetCell/Column items, which no fixture spec could express. The spec now carries `cells` and `column_widths` (see screenshot_data.json), and the capture is guarded by a filled-cell count — a sheet's row and column counts do not move when its content vanishes, so only counting cells that rendered text can see it go empty. Column headers (A/B/C) and row numbers are deliberately absent: sheet_view.cpp shows them only in edit mode. A live cell renders its item's display format (Температура shows 42.3; Активная мощность has no format and shows 125). That exposed a third bug: a formula cell cached the text it formatted when the sheet opened, and nothing notifies when an item's format arrives, so `--only sheet.png` rendered raw values where a full run rendered formatted ones — and a real sheet opened before its nodes loaded stayed unformatted for the life of the window. Formula cells now format on read (SheetCell::GetDisplayText), and the two renders agree. Populating this capture found a teardown crash: ~SheetCell erases itself from SheetModel::blinking_cells_, which was declared after `cells_` and so destroyed before them — closing a sheet holding one blinking cell segfaulted in std::set::erase, reachable by any user whose custom table binds a cell to a live value. Fixed by declaration order, with a regression test in sheet_model_unittest.cpp. It also found the alignment bug this capture now demonstrates: per-cell alignment was parsed, stored and offered in the context menu but never reached the screen, because GridCell carried no alignment and the grid adapter handed Qt the aui enum raw — so every aui::Grid in the client rendered left-aligned whatever its columns asked for. Fixed in grid_model_adapter.cpp + GridCell, with tests in grid_model_adapter_unittest.cpp; summary.png and client-retransmission.png changed with it. macOS render pending a Windows re-render; validation-only.

Objects explorer (the Struct window, ObjectTreeModel) — the operator's device/signal tree, collapsed to its top level. Only the root row keeps a glyph. macOS render pending a Windows re-render; validation-only. Published 2026-08-15 in place of `devices-on.png`, the hand-annotated composite client.md used for the object panel. What the annotation pointed at — binding a device in the group's parameters — the surrounding prose already states, but the replacement does NOT show a group's link state in the Значение column: nothing in the fixture binds a device to a group, so that column renders empty. Filed as its own backlog entry. Re-rendered dark for the published subset.

Files view (FileSystemView) — the server's file store as a tree: directories typed FileDirectoryType, files typed FileType, expanded. Untagged until 2026-08-01, so the managed-image gate skipped it, and the fixture defined no file nodes at all — the view rendered its single root row, which no row count could catch (hence min_columns' sibling fix: the tree row check now counts materialized descendants, not just top-level rows, and runs after the expand step). The fixture's file store is described under `_filesystem_comment` in screenshot_data.json; it also needed FileDirectoryType added to the shared ScadaTestAddressSpace and FileType corrected there from ObjectType to VariableType, which is what filesystem.xml declares. The expand step settles pending node loads and expands twice: the tree's leaf test resolves a node's type definition lazily, so on the first pass every file still drew an expand twisty. macOS render pending a Windows re-render; validation-only.

Data view (the TimeVal window, TimedDataModel) — one item's raw history as a value table (source timestamp / value / quality / server timestamp).
